A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ECHO research work. Their complete main texts, figures, tables, equations, and Appendices A–E are readable and support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original report-generation evaluations, component and normalization ablations, throughput measurements, and qualitative examples in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results and reports additional base-model comparison entries in Table 1.

M1.justification: The RAD adaptation, DCD trajectory collection and alignment, token reweighting, EOS supervision, report normalization, and fused KV-cache procedure are unchanged. Algorithm 1 retains the same steps.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same CXR sources, supplemental LLaVA-ReCap data, and English/Chinese report-generation coverage. Evaluation remains on MIMIC-CXR, CheXpert-Plus, and ReXGradient.

E2.justification: Table 1 adds ECHO-AR and a separate ECHOBase,blk8 comparator row; the previous ECHOBase row is identified as blk4. ECHO-AR already appeared in other analyses, but its participation in this comparison is new. The external comparator set is unchanged.

E3.justification: Table 1 changes the reference for relative quality degradation from ECHOBase to ECHO-AR, altering the comparison metric's normalization. Training settings, evaluation samples, and decoding procedures are otherwise retained. The TPF/TPS explanations added to Section 5.1.4 already appeared in v1 Appendix B.3.

E4.justification: The DCD component ablations, native one-step controls, report-normalization ablations, RAD data-scale analysis, token-confidence analysis, and appendix qualitative cases retain the same evidence and findings.

E5.justification: Repeated-run, seed, and statistical uncertainty reporting practices are unchanged. Figure 3 retains the same token-confidence variability display; no new confidence intervals or significance tests appear.

E6.justification: Table 1 adds block-size-8 base-model scores and throughput, including 52.76 TPS. ECHO-AR quality scores repeat v1 Table 4, while its throughput is now explicit. Existing methods' raw scores remain unchanged, but relative drops are recalculated: ECHO blk8's CheXpert-Plus CIDEr drop changes from 2% to 7% with the same 4.14 score and a different reference.

T1.justification: The mean-field definitions and reasoning in Section 3, mathematical objectives, and fused KV-cache FLOP derivation in Appendix E are unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract replaces 'without compromising clinical accuracy' with 'negligible degradation.' The introduction distinguishes 8× theoretical from 5.1× practical speedup and specifies that the retained 390% claim concerns the corresponding multi-step baseline at block size 8. The central methodological contributions remain unchanged.

C2.justification: Section 5.2 now interprets quality loss relative to the shared autoregressive starting model and justifies this as a common reference across block sizes. It describes blk4 as a more conservative clinical-fidelity operating point. Mechanism explanations and applicability boundaries otherwise remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Implementation details, hardware, preprocessing, hyperparameters, prompts, and access information are retained. The blk8 teacher specification emphasized in v2 Section 5.2 was already documented in v1 Appendix C.

R1.justification: The cited works and related-work positioning are unchanged, including the claimed novelty of one-step DCD distillation.

P1.justification: There are localized grammar and terminology corrections, updated date text, expanded efficiency explanations, and a rewritten comparison paragraph. The overall section structure and narrative remain intact.

P2.justification: Table 1 gains two rows and an explanatory caption; Tables 1 and 3 move to later pages. Appendix table captions change their stated percentage reference. Figures and other table structures remain unchanged, with limited pagination changes.

improvement.justification: Distinguishing theoretical from practical speedup, acknowledging small accuracy losses, and displaying the autoregressive and block-specific base models make the central efficiency comparison more transparent. These limited gains are partly offset by an appendix reporting regression: Tables A.1–A.3 now name ECHO-AR as the percentage reference while retaining their earlier ECHOBase-relative percentages. The method and most empirical evidence remain unchanged.
